newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine alliance takes cautious stance on strike.
newsitem.headline: Argentine alliance takes cautious stance on strike.

text.p: Argentina's opposition alliance on Thursday described a 24-hour strike by dissident trade unions as a success, though it took pains to stress that need to preserve economic stability.

The Radical Party-Frepaso alliance, formed earlier this month, expressed "sympathy" for the strike, called to protest Argentina's 16.1 percent unemployment and government plans for legislation to make it easier for companies to hire and fire. At the same time, oppostition leaders were careful to refrain from giving the work stoppage their outright support.

Radical Party leader Rodolfo Terragno and Carlos Alvarez, leader of the center-left Frepaso coalition, told reporters the strike appeared to have attracted strong backing, though both emphasized the need to find "alternative ways" of social protest.
"After this successful strike, the opposition unions should evaluate the direction the country is taking and see that we are a new political alternative to dialogue with," Terragno said.

The Radical Party/Frepaso alliance, whose formation has drastically altered Argentina's political landscape, has sought to reassure the electorate that it would not jeopardize Argentina's current economic stability.
More notably, it was quick to line up behind Convertibility, the policy of pegging the peso at par with the dollar. In place since 1991, the policy is credited with slowing inflation to nearly zero.
"We must not confuse Convertibility with the lack of jobs, or productivity with social injustice," Alvarez said.

Menem's government has openly blamed the alliance for the strike, which was staged by the opposition CTA and MTA union federations. It was opposed by the bigger CGT union federation, which has struck a deal on labor reforms with the government.
The alliance poses the first real challenge to Peronism in October's mid-term elections for Congress, and for the Menem succession in 1999's presidential elections.
